skill.name: lark-apps
skill.description: Deploy local HTML files or directories to Lark Miaoda, create or update apps, publish shareable URLs, and manage access scope.
skill.summary: Deploy HTML to Lark Miaoda and manage app sharing.
skill.author: larksuite

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown links, example URLs, lark-cli snippets, and defensive credential-blocklist prose. The meaningful risk is recursive HTML publishing: broad directories can include hidden or sensitive files, and some key file types are not blocked. No evidence of prompt injection or encoded payloads was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Recursive directory publishing can include unintended files.
remediation.suggestion: Default to a dedicated build output path and exclude .git, node_modules, private keys, certificate keys, and cloud config files.

remediation.issue: The --allow-sensitive bypass can publish files that validation would otherwise block.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation and show the dry-run sensitive_waived list before publishing with --allow-sensitive.

remediation.issue: Public or no-login access can make a deployed app widely visible.
remediation.suggestion: Confirm the intended audience before setting public access, especially when require-login is false.

content.user_title: Deploy HTML to Lark Miaoda Apps
content.value_statement: Publishing a local HTML demo can require app creation, upload, and sharing setup. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Lark CLI workflows for Miaoda apps.
actual_capabilities: Create Miaoda HTML apps with a name, description, and icon URL.
Publish an index.html file or build directory to a new or existing app.
Run dry-run checks to review publish payload files and size.
Update app names or descriptions while preserving other fields.
Set or read access scope for public, tenant, or specific audiences.
Extract app IDs from Miaoda URLs or user-provided app IDs.
limitations: Requires installed and authenticated lark-cli access.
Supports Miaoda HTML apps, not Lark Drive, Docs, or Slides.
Directory uploads can include unwanted files unless the output path is clean.
Specific access targets may require separate user, department, or chat lookup.

use_cases.title: Publish a Frontend Demo
use_cases.description: Deploy a clean HTML build directory to Miaoda and return a shareable app link.

use_cases.title: Manage Internal App Sharing
use_cases.description: Set an existing app to tenant-wide, public, or specific-user visibility.

use_cases.title: Share a Prototype Quickly
use_cases.description: Create a new Miaoda app from a local prototype and prepare it for stakeholder review.

prompt_templates.title: Publish a Local Demo
prompt_templates.prompt: Deploy my ./dist HTML build to Miaoda and return the shareable URL.

prompt_templates.title: Create and Share a New App
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Miaoda HTML app named Customer Survey, publish ./dist, and tell me the final URL.

prompt_templates.title: Update Access for a Team
prompt_templates.prompt: Set this Miaoda app to company-wide access and report the final visibility setting.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Then Publish a Build Directory
prompt_templates.prompt: Dry-run publish ./build, review the payload for risky files, then publish only if the output is clean.

output_examples.input: Publish the dist folder as a shareable Miaoda app.
output_examples.output: The assistant creates a Miaoda HTML app, publishes the clean dist directory, and returns the app URL with sharing notes.

output_examples.input: Make this app available to everyone in my company.
output_examples.output: The assistant sets the access scope to tenant-wide and confirms the app is visible to the organization.
The assistant explains the validation or API hint and suggests a concrete fix before another publish attempt.

best_practices: Publish from a dedicated build directory that contains only required web assets.
Run a dry-run before public publishing or when the payload is unfamiliar.
Confirm the intended audience before enabling public or no-login access.
anti_patterns: Publishing the project root when a smaller build directory is available.
Using --allow-sensitive without explicit user intent and a reviewed dry-run result.
Enumerating existing apps when the user can provide a Miaoda URL or app ID.

faq.question: What does this skill publish?
faq.answer: It publishes local HTML files or directories as Miaoda HTML apps through lark-cli.

faq.question: Does it create new apps?
faq.answer: Yes. It can create a new Miaoda HTML app when the user does not provide an app ID.

faq.question: Can it update existing app metadata?
faq.answer: Yes. It can update an app name or description while leaving other fields unchanged.

faq.question: Can it control who can access an app?
faq.answer: Yes. It can set public, tenant-wide, or specific-audience access scopes.

faq.question: What files should I publish?
faq.answer: Use a clean build output directory with index.html and only the files required by the app.

faq.question: Does it replace Lark Drive or Docs skills?
faq.answer: No. It is for Miaoda HTML apps, not ordinary cloud files, documents, or native slides.
